reason: Ligular (ligulate) means strap-shaped, as in ray florets. It could also mean 'of the ligule', so a few rows may be wrong.
'Narrow' is lost. Ovate is also a 2-D shape, while ovoid is 3-D. Keep this for the pending ovate/ovoid classes or leave it unmapped.
Narrowing gradually to a point is the meaning of tapered.
'Nearly solid' means a small cavity or pith is present. 'Not hollow' states that the part is fully solid.
'Angled' (stems, twigs) means angular, so 'not angled' is not angular.
'Not distinctly developed' is about the degree of development, not visibility. Inconspicuous is the wrong meaning.
'Not prickly' means prickles are absent, so prickle absent is right.
Negated scaly.
Not strophiolate means the strophiole is absent.
Verrucose means warty, so 'not verrucose' is not warty.
Obscurely visible (veins, glands) means inconspicuous.
Trigonous is three-angled. Only the bluntness of the angles is lost, which is a small detail.
'Pealike' means resembling a pea in shape or in the pea family. It is not the size class pea-sized.
Premorose means ending as if bitten off and ragged, which is close to erose.
Prickleless means no prickles.
Decumbent means lying on the ground with the tips ascending, which is what prostrate-ascending describes.
Ramentaceous means covered with ramenta, which are chaffy scales.
Rancid is an unpleasant, offensive odour. The class definition is general enough to cover it.
A part that detaches readily falls off easily, which is deciduous or caducous.
Sacciform means shaped like a sac, which is saccate.
Sclerenchyma is present. The 'in strands' arrangement is lost, but presence is still true.
Semi-embracing means partly clasping (semi-amplexicaul).
Sparsely distributed means sparse.
'Stellate' means opening by star-shaped slits. Plain dehiscent loses the opening mode.
This is a shape between lanceolate and triangular. The order of the words differs slightly.
'Transversely' means wider than long (oriented across the part). Elliptic loses this orientation.
Pitted means foveate, so unpitted is not foveate.
'Winding' for a stem of a climber means twining, not sinuous. It is sinuous only for veins, margins and similar parts.
'With blade' also applies to petals, sepals and tepals, whose blades are not the leaf lamina.
Without buds means no buds.
Cilia are marginal hairs only. Trichome absent says there are no hairs of any kind.
'Without distinct blade' means the blade is indistinct or reduced. It does not mean the lamina is absent.
Without hairs means glabrous.
Without a mucro means not mucronate.
Without multicellular hairs means multicellular trichomes are absent.
Multiseptate hairs are multicellular. Absence of the multiseptate type does not rule out two-celled hairs.
Without teeth means not dentate.
'Woody' (a liana habit) is lost. Climbing alone also covers herbaceous climbers.
'Alike' is only 'not dimorphic' when it refers to morphs (e.g. both sexes or both flower types alike). Otherwise it means similar.
Channelled means grooved.
Closely set means close together, which is approximate.
Different lengths means unequal in size.
'Equally developed' is about the degree of development, not equal size. The equal class is a size quality.
Furrowless means not furrowed.
Heterostyled is the same as heterostylous.
Negated pubescent.
This is the same word with a hyphen.
Regularly distributed means a regular spatial pattern.
Reticulately veined means reticulate venation.
A sabre shape is a curved blade, close to falciform (sickle-shaped).
